rule: Direct payments involve exactly 2 banks; Indirect and Covered payments involve 3 or more
test: share of rows where (type = Direct) <=> (PARTICIPANT_COUNT = 2), full data
interpretation: Direct = the two banks hold accounts with each other; otherwise correspondent banks relay the payment

rule: The number of intermediary banks is geometric: each further intermediary is added with probability q = 0.368; Indirect and Covered share the same hop distribution
test: total variation distance between observed and geometric distribution of PARTICIPANT_COUNT - 2, full data
interpretation: Banks use the shortest correspondent chain available, so each extra hop is rarer

rule: PARTICIPANT_COUNT = number of BIC entries on the path, repeated BICs counted (complete paths)
test: share of rows without a path gap where path_len = PARTICIPANT_COUNT, full data
interpretation: A bank that handles the payment twice counts twice

rule: The path starts at the ordering BIC and ends at the beneficiary BIC; in ~5% of rows each end is a different (usually foreign) bank
test: share of rows, full data, every routing type
interpretation: A parent/branch BIC or an outsourced sending/receiving bank processes the payment

rule: Observed continuity-gap ('...') frequencies are consistent with a model in which each link independently has about a 5.0% chance of a gap: it fits every path length within sampling error (independence itself is not proven)
test: chi-square goodness of fit: observed gap rate vs 1-(1-q)^(participants-1) for every path length with >= 1000 rows (q from Direct rows only), full data
value: goodness of fit chi-square 13.5 on 8 df, p = 0.10; largest error 0.0139 (|z| = 2.4)
interpretation: Longer chains have more hand-overs where tracking can break

rule: Routing type has negligible measured association with the business/consumer pair (not proof of independent assignment)
test: Cramér's V (routing type x pair), full data
interpretation: Routing patterns are very similar across B/C pair types; the data do not identify whether customer type enters the generator directly

rule: Domestic payments are routed Covered more often than cross-border ones; the Direct share is the same
test: Covered share domestic vs cross-border; Cramér's V, full data
interpretation: Counter-intuitive (cover payments are normally cross-border): likely a feature of how the data was generated

rule: Median duration rises with routing type (Direct < Indirect < Covered) and with every extra bank on the path
test: median duration by type and hop count (normal rows, full data); R² of ln(duration) on type + hops (20% sample)
interpretation: Plausibly each correspondent bank adds processing and queueing time (not observed directly)

rule: Sender and receiver country each add their own delay, about as much as routing does
test: R² of ln(duration) on sender + receiver country, Direct payments only (additive, 20% sample)
interpretation: Plausibly each country's banks have their own processing speed (cut-off times, compliance checks); the cause is not identified in the data

rule: Scam payments take longer than normal payments with the same routing type and hop count; fat-finger and duplicate payments barely differ
test: median duration ratio vs normal payments with the same routing type and hop count (Mann-Whitney), full data
value: same routing: ACCOUNT_REPLACEMENT_SCAM x5.8; CEO_SCAM x7.7; DUPLICATE_PAYMENT x1.3; FAT_FINGER_MISTAKE x1.0; ROMANCE_SCAM x13.9 | unadjusted: ROMANCE_SCAM x20.5; CEO_SCAM x13.2; ACCOUNT_REPLACEMENT_SCAM x10.2
interpretation: Consistent with a screening hold before release, but the hold itself is not observed: a plausible mechanism, not a proven cause

rule: Sender-local hour / weekday changes duration
test: extra R² of ln(duration) beyond type + hops
interpretation: In the fitted model, inferred local hour and weekday add negligible explanatory power; a zero causal effect is not established

rule: Conversions = number of local-currency changes between consecutive banks on the path (payment currency not counted)
test: exact prediction accuracy, 20% sample, paths without a gap
interpretation: Each bank converts only when it hands the payment to a bank in another currency zone; extends R-CCY2 and R-CCY3

rule: Conversions also count the change from the payment currency to the first bank
test: exact prediction accuracy, same rows
interpretation: The first bank does not convert the payment currency

rule: R-CCY2 exceptions disappear when the banks actually on the path are used instead of the ordering/beneficiary BIC
test: accuracy on all Direct rows, full data
interpretation: Conversions follow the banks that process the payment (see R-RT2)

rule: At the same routing and hop count, extra conversions add duration
test: extra R² of conversions on ln(duration) given type + hops
interpretation: After adjusting for type and hop count, FX conversions add negligible explanatory power in the tested model; a causal zero effect is not proven

rule: Fat-finger-labelled payments are disproportionately extreme in size versus comparable normal payments; an exact x10^k mechanism is not established
test: share of payments whose rounded log10 distance from the country x pair median is >= 2 (about 32x or more)
interpretation: Consistent with a keying slip that multiplies the amount by a power of 10

rule: Duplicates come in bursts of 2-5 identical payments (same sender, payee, currency and amount) about 18 minutes apart; every copy in these bursts is labelled, and an earlier unlabelled match is found no more often than by chance (no evidence of unlabelled originals)
test: burst structure of labelled duplicates; share with an earlier matching payment vs normal payments
value: 185 bursts of 2-5 copies, identical amount 100%, median 1099s apart; first copy with an earlier unlabelled match 9.2% (normal 9.2%); earlier match (any copy): 75.6% vs 9.4% control (diff +66.1% [+62.4%, +69.9%], p < 1e-300); 74.6% vs 8.3% control (diff +66.4% [+58.8%, +73.9%], p = 1.1e-87)
interpretation: Consistent with a back-office re-submission of the same instruction

rule: Business and consumer duplicates follow the same pattern: re-sent by the same sender, minutes later. The hypothesised consumer pattern (a different sender, hours or days later) is not found
test: same-sender share and gap to the matched original, by sender type (duplicates with a match)
interpretation: One re-submission pattern for both sender types; the B/C split in hypothesis A2 is not supported

rule: Romance scam: one consumer pays the same consumer several times within a day, with rising amounts
test: C2C pairs with 3+ payments: rising amounts and within-1-day share vs normal pairs
interpretation: Consistent with a victim being groomed into sending more and more

rule: CEO scam: business sender, first payment to a new payee, amount above the usual level
test: first-time payee share vs normal business payments; amount shift (Mann-Whitney)
interpretation: Consistent with a fake executive ordering an urgent transfer to a new supplier account

rule: Account-replacement scams: no earlier payment from the same sender to the same payee was found (exact party text, or first name line); the replacement mechanism is not recovered with these matching methods
test: earlier payment from the same sender (BIC8 + account) to the same payee: exact party text, then relaxed first-line name match (4.6b); the same exact-text match finds a predecessor for normal payments, so the method can find links
value: 0.0% vs 5.7% control (diff -5.7% [-6.4%, -5.1%], p = 3.7e-10); relaxed name match 0.2% [0.0%, 0.9%], n = 649, with a changed account 1
interpretation: The label is not tied to a payee history that these joins can see; names or details may be re-generated, so absence of a match does not prove absence of a link

rule: For labels outside the appendix (CUSTOMER_RECALL), no linked payment (same sender and receiver bank + account, amount +-1%) was found for almost all rows
test: share of these rows with no matching payment (observation only)
interpretation: Observation only: how recalls arise is unresolved (the label is not defined in the appendix; ask the organisers)

rule: Anomaly rates are not uniform: they differ by conversions, cross_border, hour_utc, pair, transaction_type, weekday_utc; no difference by qflag
test: chi-square per anomaly x segment (p < 0.001 counted)
value: 14 of 42 anomaly x segment tests significant: conversions, cross_border, hour_utc, pair, transaction_type, weekday_utc
interpretation: Each scam type concentrates in its own segments; the cause is not identified

rule: IBAN is used for every account of a bank country or for none; IBAN country = BIC country
test: countries with mixed formats; IBAN country match
value: 76 countries all-IBAN, 153 none, 0 mixed; country match 100.00%
interpretation: IBAN is a national standard, adopted country by country

rule: Non-IBAN account numbers that contain a currency code use the bank country's local currency
test: share of non-IBAN accounts with a 3-letter code; match
value: 13.3% contain a code; 99.6% of those = local currency
interpretation: Domestic account numbers often carry the account currency

rule: Each sender account number belongs to one bank and one party type; 2.4% of receiver account numbers recur under several banks, so every account history uses (BIC8, account)
test: share of account numbers with > 1 BIC / party type
interpretation: Account numbers are issued per bank, so the same number can exist at two banks

rule: Party details lines are at most 35 characters (SWIFT MT line format)
test: share of details texts with every line <= 35 characters
interpretation: The 4 x 35 character field of SWIFT MT messages

rule: Business parties get company-name tokens; consumers get person-name tokens
test: share by party type
value: receiver B business 87.7%; receiver C person 90.8%
interpretation: Consistent with a name generator that depends on the party type

rule: Sender address country = sender bank country; the receiver's address country usually differs
test: share of address country = bank country
interpretation: Consistent with senders banking locally while receivers can live anywhere

rule: The numbered (1/2/3/ lines) and BIC-line formats never occur in the same details text; the other 80% match neither (free text: a residual class, not a tested third template)
test: share of details texts matching BOTH explicit formats (the rule predicts 0), both sides, full data
value: beneficiary: numbered 15.0%, BIC line 5.0%, neither (free text) 80.0%, both 0.000%; ordering: numbered 16.0%, BIC line 5.0%, neither (free text) 79.0%, both 0.000%
interpretation: Consistent with one format being chosen per party text; regex classes describe the text and do not show how the free text is generated

rule: No detectable difference in the trailing finance / stop-word line rate between any anomaly type and normal payments (gaps of up to about 3 points cannot be excluded)
test: difference in the share with a filler line, each anomaly type vs all normal payments (two-proportion z-test)
value: largest difference 3.3 points; 0 of 12 comparisons with p < 0.001, 1 with p < 0.05
interpretation: Consistent with filler text that carries no anomaly information; this does not show how the filler is generated or that it is random

rule: The payment currency is the local currency of the first bank on the path (usually the ordering bank)
test: full data; local currency = modal sender currency per BIC country, inferred in-sample (holdout checks in notebook 01)
value: first path bank 93.4%; ordering bank 89.4%; receiver-only 4.2% (18.9% match the receiver currency incl. same-currency pairs); N = 10,000,000
interpretation: The bank that sends the payment debits in its home currency; FX happens later along the route

rule: Direct payments: 1 conversion if sender and receiver local currencies differ, otherwise 0
test: prediction accuracy on all Direct rows
interpretation: With only two banks, FX happens once, and only between currency areas

rule: Conversions never exceed the number of hops (participants - 1)
test: share of all rows
interpretation: Each correspondent bank can convert at most once

rule: Amounts are approximately log-normal given sender country and party types: the ln residual has near-zero skew and kurtosis and the same spread for every pair
test: skew / excess kurtosis / sd of ln residual (an approximation; not proof of the exact generating distribution)
interpretation: Consistent with payment sizes built from many multiplying factors; the exact distribution is not established

rule: Each business party (sender or receiver) multiplies the amount by e^2 = 7.4
test: ln effect within sender country, 95% cluster-bootstrap CI
interpretation: Businesses pay invoices and payroll; consumers send small personal transfers

rule: The sender's country sets the base amount; the receiver's country adds a negligible amount (extra R² below 0.01)
test: R² sender country vs extra R² of receiver country
interpretation: The sending BIC country sets the typical payment size; why (e.g. income levels) cannot be tested with the competition data

rule: Sender and receiver party types have a negligible association on all 9,992,994 normal payments (consistent with independent assignment; not proof of independent draws)
test: Cramér's V and P(receiver B) by sender type, all normal rows; chi-square p naive and clustered by sender account
value: V = 0.0010; P(receiver B) 28.84% for B vs 28.73% for C senders; p = 0.003 naive, 0.595 account-clustered
interpretation: Consistent with separate draws for who pays and who gets paid

rule: On each sender country's inferred clock, payments follow an office-hours rhythm; business and consumer timing is nearly the same
test: share 07:00-19:59 on the data-inferred local clock vs UTC; V(hour, sender type)
interpretation: Consistent with payments entered in office hours. The clock offsets were inferred assuming a Mon-Fri week, so the pattern is partly built into them: not verified time zones
verdict_raw: Strong (clock offsets inferred from the data)

rule: Business sender accounts send more payments than consumer accounts
test: payments per (sender BIC, account) over the whole 3-month window (the ratio depends on window length: about x3.8 within 30 days)
interpretation: Consistent with companies paying many suppliers and staff (not observed directly)

rule: CEO scams only come from business senders; romance scams only from consumer senders
test: labelled anomalies by sender type (full data)
value: CEO: B 945, C 0; romance: B 0, C 2476
interpretation: Each scam targets a specific kind of victim

rule: Handout example: consonant currency codes give 3x amounts
test: ln residual difference consonant - vowel (3x would be +1.099)
interpretation: The handout example is illustrative, not a rule in this dataset

rule: Cross-border payments are smaller than domestic ones
test: raw median ratio vs within-country ln effect
value: raw x0.62; same country and party types x1.00
interpretation: Confounding: domestic payments are concentrated in sender countries with higher typical amounts; within the same country and party types the cross-border effect is negligible

rule: Paying in a non-local currency changes the amount
test: ln residual difference non-local - local

rule: Transaction type, hour or weekday changes the amount
test: R² of ln amount
